story: At 11:17 on a breezy, clear Monday in Sumter Oaks, Gary sits focused in his garage, zip-tying the wiring harness on his golf cart and testing each light strip and speaker connection with a multimeter. Down the road, Donna heads out to Magnolia Loop with an optimistic spring in her step, while Hal, determined as ever, stands on the street counting the flamingos in Donna's flock and checking his tally against the L-02 record. Back at home, Rosa makes a determined decision of her own: she pens "Coffee with Hal" in ink on one open morning this week and sets aside the chair for him.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Zip-tie the wiring harness and check each light strip and speaker connection with the multimeter
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and check the tally against L-02
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Pick one open morning this week, write 'Coffee with Hal' in ink, and save the chair for him

gary.thought_process: Last tick I grabbed zip ties and a multimeter from the toolbox. The harness is run and the light strips are mounted, so now I secure the wiring and test every connection before the parade. I need to keep L-03 in mind: it's 11 AM, so a low-volume speaker test is fine. L-04 means holiday lighting is okay from Thanksgiving on, and L-01 says exterior mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, so I should file that at Town Hall soon. For now, finish the wiring work on the cart. Nobody's around, so I can just get on with it.

parameters.content: Zip-tie the wiring harness and check each light strip and speaker connection with the multimeter

donna.thought_process: I've already penciled in the Tuesday court slot, packed the bag, and texted Gary the time. The planning is done, so there's nothing more to do with the calendar or the bag. Hal is watching the flamingo count, and I've been hauling them behind the hedge all afternoon, so I'd better head out to Magnolia Loop and make sure exactly three stay visible. Staying put won't move anything forward.

parameters.content: Heading out to check the flamingo count from the street and see who's about before Tuesday's pickleball.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with my notebook full of observations and nobody in sight. The flamingo flock object is right here in the zone, and Donna's count is never what she claims. I'll check it myself, up close and by the book, before I file anything with the committee. The Halloween parade is over, so Gary's cart and the lights need a fair look too, but the flamingos come first since I'm standing right at them.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and check the tally against L-02

rosa.thought_process: I've asked myself to check my shifts for coffee with Hal four ticks running and keep circling it. Time to stop dithering and actually open the schedule, pick a morning, and commit. The dinner went well and I don't want the coffee to slip away. Nobody's around, so interacting with the schedule is the right move.

parameters.content: Pick one open morning this week, write 'Coffee with Hal' in ink, and save the chair for him

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
